name: Wrong factual claim drove one reviewer's criticism
definition: A reviewer in one committee based a criticism or a lower score on a checkable factual claim about the paper or its prior work that was wrong, and the other committee had no reviewer making that error.
exemplar: In A, Reviewer_A5qv doubted the conceptual gain because a d^2 SQ bound 'follows from DKS17', but the paper credits that bound to DKS19, which needs unknown covariance and does not transfer; after the rebuttal A5qv raised to 7, while B never raised this doubt.

name: Area chair set the award above reviewers' scores
definition: One committee's area chair recommended a higher tier than its reviewers' ratings and arguments supported, on the chair's own reading, often with a meta-review that overstates reviewer consensus.
exemplar: Committee A's chair gave a spotlight over ratings 6, 6, 6, 7 at confidence 2 to 3 with no reviewer arguing for an award, writing that 'the reviewers and I are all in agreement that the results are strong' when only Reviewer_hyJf said so.

name: Enthusiastic low-confidence review carried weight
definition: One committee had a reviewer whose high score rested on enthusiasm rather than specifics, often at low confidence, and that score or wording raised the committee's ratings or shaped its meta-review.
exemplar: In B, Reviewer_PKyu gave a praise-only 8 at confidence 2 while 'not very familiar with the topic', called the limitations discussion 'impeccable', and the meta-review copied PKyu's wording almost verbatim.

name: Authors disclosed a flaw to one committee only
definition: The authors revealed an error or weakness in the paper on one committee's forum and not on the other's, so the two committees judged different information.
exemplar: The authors disclosed on B's forum that Theorem 1.1 omitted a sqrt(t·R(U∞)) term, but their reply the same day to Reviewer_ab3Y's early-stopping question on A's forum did not mention it.

name: Committee discounted a known substantive flaw
definition: One committee learned of a substantive flaw, raised by a reviewer or admitted by the authors, yet its scores and meta-review did not weigh it, accepting a fix on trust or ignoring it.
exemplar: B learned that Theorem 1.1 as submitted was wrong and the fix changed the stated rates, yet Reviewer_9b2J wrote 'I have to trust that the proofs in appendix will be fine', no score fell, and the meta-review did not mention it.

name: Rebuttal moved scores in one committee only
definition: The authors' rebuttal led one committee's reviewers to raise or lower their scores while the other committee's scores did not move, widening or narrowing the gap between them.
exemplar: In B, Reviewer_sDSa (confidence 4) raised from 7 to 8 after the rebuttal, while no reviewer in A stated a score change.

name: One committee raised an issue the other missed
definition: A reviewer or the area chair in one committee raised a substantive, checkable concern about the paper that no one in the other committee raised, so the two committees weighed different sets of problems.
exemplar: In B, Reviewer_i9rh showed that the conclusion's claim that guidance narrows the sampling-time gap rests only on Table 4's 25-step rows, and B's AC flagged a possible interaction between the ImageNet guidance classifier and FID; no one in A raised either.

name: Committees weighted the same weakness differently
definition: Both committees identified the same substantive weakness, but one treated it as minor or a revision item while the other treated it as grounds for a lower tier or rejection.
exemplar: Reviewers in both committees found the experiments thin (two toy benchmarks, only NODE and a penalty baseline, no spread on the gas result); A accepted this as 'can be further improved' and gave a spotlight, while B rejected on 'insufficient empirical evidence'.

name: Area chair deferred to one reviewer
definition: One committee's area chair resolved split reviews by adopting a single reviewer's position without stating an assessment of their own, so one reviewer set the outcome.
exemplar: B's final positions were 3/6/7/5, and the two-sentence meta-review rejected because 'one reviewer is still strongly convinced about rejection', without weighing the two accept-side reviewers.

name: Reviewer moved after reading the other reviews
definition: A reviewer in one committee changed their score because of the other reviewers' reviews rather than new evidence from the paper or the rebuttal, pulling the committee toward the others' position.
exemplar: In B, Reviewer_DeZu cut 7 to 6, citing 'the weaknesses in the experiments section as other reviewers have noted', and offered to return to 7.

name: Authors' replies misread or missed a reviewer
definition: In one committee the authors misread a reviewer's question or left a reviewer's follow-up unanswered, which lowered or held down that reviewer's score.
exemplar: The authors misread Reviewer_AB4a's degeneracy question twice and AB4a dropped 6 to 5; DeZu offered to return to 7 and the authors never replied.

name: Thin, unengaged review entered the decision
definition: One committee had a reviewer whose score rested on assertion rather than specifics and who did not engage with the rebuttal or discussion, and that score counted in the decision unchallenged.
exemplar: In B, Reviewer_D146 gave 5 after 2 hours on the assertion that 'learning entropy growth is not as exciting' and never replied to the authors' response.

name: Area chair rejected against a positive majority
definition: One committee's area chair recommended a lower tier or rejection than most of its reviewers' final ratings supported, with no score moving to back the decision.
exemplar: A's AC rejected over final ratings 6, 7, 5, 6 with no score moved, ruling that 'the technical contributions and the writing quality do not meet the bar of NeurIPS'.

name: Area chair applied score threshold over own view
definition: One committee's area chair stated a positive assessment of the paper but decided by whether the reviewers' average score cleared the acceptance threshold, so a borderline mean set the outcome instead of the chair's reading.
exemplar: Committee A's chair called the paper 'generally solid' with results 'reasonably strong' but rejected it as 'still slightly below' the bar because no score rose above a mean of 5.4.

name: Low score held on a peripheral point
definition: A reviewer in one committee kept a below-threshold score on a point peripheral to the paper's contribution, such as a variant or detail the method does not use, after the authors had answered it, and that score counted in the decision.
exemplar: In A, Reviewer_Tk2H kept its 5 over the Gaussian-prior loss variant, which the method does not use, after the authors posted a three-model table and an alpha sweep, and that 5 was one of A's three sub-threshold ratings.

name: Committees judged different kinds of contribution
definition: The two committees evaluated the paper as different kinds of contribution, for example an application or tool for a field against a methodological advance, and so asked different questions and applied different standards to the same results.
exemplar: A's reviewers read DBE as a tool for behavioural neuroscience and rewarded its 26-point gain over BehaveNet with 8, 7, 7, 7, while B's reviewers read it as a methods paper, found the full model trails DisAE+VAME (79.53 against 81.25 accuracy), and B's AC advised reframing it 'as a study of different representations'.

name: Rebuttal persuaded reviewers who could not check core
definition: In one committee, reviewers who said the technical core was outside their expertise raised their scores on the rebuttal's clarifications and promised revisions, without new results or a check of the proofs, which lifted that committee's ratings.
exemplar: In A, Reviewer_cSRr ('unable to assess the soundness', confidence 2) and Reviewer_g3MG ('a bit beyond my expertise') raised to 7 after the authors restated the problem and listed planned changes, and those 7s carried the spotlight.

name: Committees held one paper type to different bars
definition: Both committees read the paper as the same kind of contribution, but one required it to deliver something the other did not ask of that kind of paper, such as practical guidance from an analysis study, and judged it against that extra requirement.
exemplar: All four of B's reviewers faulted the ViT-against-CNN analysis for giving no practical guidance for architecture design, and B rejected, while no one in A asked for it and A's Reviewer_qxEj praised the work because it 'might inspire new architectures'.

name: Wrong factual claim inflated one reviewer's praise
definition: A reviewer in one committee based praise or a higher score on a checkable factual claim about the paper's novelty or results that was wrong, such as crediting the authors with a method the paper itself attributes to prior work.
exemplar: In B, Reviewer_YH9r (1 hour, confidence 2) gave 7 and named 'a new algorithm', the forward algorithm, as the key contribution, but line 13 of the paper credits it to Vovk and to Azoury and Warmuth (2001).

name: Reviewer kept score after main concern answered
definition: A reviewer in one committee acknowledged that the rebuttal resolved the concern their score rested on, yet kept the same below-threshold score by citing new or secondary grounds, so the correction did not change the committee's ratings.
exemplar: In B, Reviewer_CnYk said the rebuttal's correction of the parser misreading 'answered my major concern', then kept 4 on new grounds, closed GPT-3 and novelty.

name: Promised revisions credited by one committee only
definition: One committee judged the paper as submitted and refused to credit comparisons, experiments or fixes the authors only promised in the rebuttal, while the other committee accepted such promises or did not require them.
exemplar: A's chair rejected because the MMD and KCpA comparison and fair kernel experiments existed only as rebuttal promises, writing that the comparison 'should not happen in the authors' response'; B accepted with the same gaps.

name: Reviewer's stated stance diverged from score
definition: A reviewer in one committee stated a changed position in a comment, such as now leaning to accept, but never edited the score, and the committee acted on the stated position rather than the rating.
exemplar: In B, the only detractor, Reviewer_hFCk, wrote 'I now lean to accept this paper' after the rebuttal but kept its 5, and B accepted with a spotlight as if no reviewer opposed.

name: Off-record extra reviewer broke a split panel
definition: One committee's area chair called in an additional reviewer late in the process, whose review is not on the record for the authors or the other reviewers, and used that input to decide a split panel.
exemplar: A's visible ratings were 8, 5, 5 with the most engaged detractor 'not opposed to acceptance'; the AC 'collected additional feedback from an emergency reviewer' who 'shared the same concerns' and rejected 'based on this input and the discussions'.

name: Reviewer expertise shaped clarity verdicts
definition: The committees' reviewers stood at different distances from the paper's field, so reviewers outside the field found the exposition unclear and penalised it, while a domain expert in the other committee read the same text as clear.
exemplar: A's Reviewer_oT7u 'had to read into related work' to follow the method and asked for rejection over the rewrite, while B's computational-anatomy expert xE8n called the paper well written.
